title: One gradient step, by hand
summary: Fill in a gradient-descent update and what happens when the step is too large.
text: The loss is $L(w) = (w - 3)^2$, so $\frac{dL}{dw} = 2(w - 3)$. At $w = 5$ the gradient is [[grad]]. One gradient-descent step with learning rate $\eta = 0.1$ moves $w$ to [[w_new]]. The update subtracts the gradient because the gradient points in the direction where the loss [[direction]]. With $\eta = 1.5$, the same step lands at $w =$ [[w_big]], further from the minimum than where it started.
